subject: maths
title: Introduction to Trigonometry
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Every answer shows the working. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: If sin A = 3/5, then cos A is —
questions.work:
Opposite = 3, hypotenuse = 5 ⇒ adjacent = √(25 − 9) = 4.
cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse = 4/5. (Or cos²A = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25.)

questions.q: If k + 7 sec²52° − 7 tan²52° = 7, then k is —
(sin²22° + sin²68°)/(cos²22° + cos²68°) + sin²63° + cos 63° sin 27° is —
questions.work:
sin 68° = cos 22° and cos 68° = sin 22°, so the fraction = (sin²22° + cos²22°)/(cos²22° + sin²22°) = 1.
sin 27° = cos 63°, so sin²63° + cos 63° sin 27° = sin²63° + cos²63° = 1.
Total = 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.q: In △ABC right-angled at B, AB = 12 cm and BC = 5 cm. Then sin C is —
questions.work:
AC = √(144 + 25) = 13.
For angle C the opposite side is AB = 12, so sin C = 12/13.

questions.q: cosec²67° − tan²23° + 1 is —
questions.work:
cosec 67° = sec(90° − 67°) = sec 23°.
sec²23° − tan²23° = 1, so the value is 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.q: If tan 2A = cot(A − 18°), where 2A is acute, then A is —
If 3 tan A = 4, then cos A is —
questions.work:
tan A = 4/3: opposite 4, adjacent 3, hypotenuse 5.
cos A = 3/5.

questions.q: If sin θ + sin²θ = 1, then cos²θ + cos⁴θ is —
questions.work:
sin θ = 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ.
So cos²θ + cos⁴θ = sin θ + sin²θ = 1.

questions.q: (tan 50° + sec 50°)/(cot 40° + cosec 40°) + cos 40° cosec 50° is —
questions.work:
tan 50° = cot 40° and sec 50° = cosec 40°, so the fraction = 1.
cosec 50° = sec 40°, so cos 40° cosec 50° = cos 40° × 1/cos 40° = 1.
Total = 2.

questions.q: sin(45° + θ) − cos(45° − θ) is —
questions.work:
cos(45° − θ) = sin(90° − (45° − θ)) = sin(45° + θ).
So the difference is 0.

questions.q: cos²75° − sin²15° is —
If 4 tan θ = 3, then cosec θ is —
questions.work:
tan θ = 3/4: opposite 3, adjacent 4, hypotenuse 5.
sin θ = 3/5 ⇒ cosec θ = 5/3.

questions.q: (sin A + cos A)² − 2 sin A cos A is —
questions.work:
(sin A + cos A)² = sin²A + cos²A + 2 sin A cos A.
Subtract 2 sin A cos A: sin²A + cos²A = 1.

questions.q: cot²A − 1/sin²A is —
questions.work: 1/sin²A = cosec²A, and cot²A − cosec²A = −(cosec²A − cot²A) = −1.

questions.q: sin⁴A − cos⁴A is —
questions.work: sin⁴A − cos⁴A = (sin²A − cos²A)(sin²A + cos²A) = sin²A − cos²A = (1 − cos²A) − cos²A = 1 − 2cos²A.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) 3 sin 19°/cos 71° = ____. (ii) sec 41° sin 49° + cos 49° cosec 41° = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) cos 71° = sin 19°, so 3 sin 19°/sin 19° = 3.
(ii) sin 49° = cos 41°, so sec 41° sin 49° = 1; cos 49° = sin 41°, so cos 49° cosec 41° = 1. Total 2.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks (any two): (i) If sec θ = 5/4, tan²θ/(1 + tan²θ) = ____. (ii) cos A sin(90° − A) + sin A cos(90° − A) = ____. (iii) If cos θ + sin θ = √2 cos θ, tan θ = ____. (iv) sec²57° − cot²33° − tan²45° = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) tan²θ/sec²θ = sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ = 1 − 16/25 = 9/25.
(ii) cos A × cos A + sin A × sin A = 1.
(iii) sin θ = (√2 − 1) cos θ ⇒ tan θ = √2 − 1.
(iv) cot 33° = tan 57°, so sec²57° − tan²57° − 1 = 1 − 1 = 0.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: (ii) sec θ(1 − sin θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = ____. Also, (i) cos 47° cot 79° − sin 43° tan 11° = ____.
questions.answer:
(ii) sec θ(1 − sin θ) = sec θ − tan θ; (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.
(i) cos 47° = sin 43° and cot 79° = tan 11°, so the two terms are equal: 0.

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) sin 10θ = cos 8θ (10θ acute) gives tan 9θ = 1. (ii) The value of sin A can be 4/3.
questions.answer:
(i) True: 10θ + 8θ = 90° ⇒ θ = 5° ⇒ tan 45° = 1.
(ii) False: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse ≤ 1.

sections.title: Case study: read the information and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: The length of the ramp is —
questions.work: Ramp = hypotenuse = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 m.

questions.q: sin θ is —
questions.work: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5.

questions.q: cos θ is —
questions.work: cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = 4/5.

questions.q: tan θ is —
questions.work: tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 3/4.

questions.q: sin²θ + cos²θ equals —
questions.work: 9/25 + 16/25 = 25/25 = 1, as the identity says.

sections.passage: A ramp for wheelchairs rises 3 m over a horizontal distance of 4 m. Let θ be the angle the ramp makes with the ground.

questions.q: If cos θ = 4/5, find (1 − sin θ tan θ)/(2 tan²θ).
questions.answer:
Adjacent 4, hypotenuse 5 ⇒ opposite 3: sin θ = 3/5, tan θ = 3/4.
Numerator = 1 − (3/5)(3/4) = 1 − 9/20 = 11/20.
Denominator = 2 × 9/16 = 9/8.
Value = (11/20) × (8/9) = 22/45.

questions.q: Prove that √((1 − cos²θ) sec²θ) = tan θ.
questions.answer:
1 − cos²θ = sin²θ, and sec²θ = 1/cos²θ.
√(sin²θ/cos²θ) = sin θ/cos θ = tan θ (θ acute).

questions.q: Prove that (1 − cos A)/(1 + cos A) = (cot A − cosec A)².
questions.answer:
Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 − cos A):
(1 − cos A)²/(1 − cos²A) = (1 − cos A)²/sin²A = ((1 − cos A)/sin A)² = (cosec A − cot A)² = (cot A − cosec A)².

questions.q: Prove that √((1 − sin A)/(1 + sin A)) = sec A − tan A.
questions.answer:
Multiply inside by (1 − sin A)/(1 − sin A):
√((1 − sin A)²/(1 − sin²A)) = √((1 − sin A)²/cos²A) = (1 − sin A)/cos A = sec A − tan A.

questions.q: Prove that (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ)/(1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ) = 1.
questions.answer:
sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)² − 2 sin²θ cos²θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ.
So the fraction equals 1.

questions.q: Show that tan 48° tan 23° tan 42° tan 67° = 1.
questions.answer:
tan 42° = cot 48° and tan 67° = cot 23°.
The product = (tan 48° cot 48°)(tan 23° cot 23°) = 1 × 1 = 1.

questions.q: Given tan A = 4/3, find sin A and cos A.
questions.answer:
Opposite 4, adjacent 3, hypotenuse √(16 + 9) = 5.
sin A = 4/5, cos A = 3/5.

questions.q: If cos θ = 7/25, find sin θ and tan θ.
questions.answer:
Adjacent 7, hypotenuse 25 ⇒ opposite √(625 − 49) = 24.
sin θ = 24/25, tan θ = 24/7.

questions.q: Prove that cos⁴A − sin⁴A = 1 − 2 sin²A.
questions.answer: cos⁴A − sin⁴A = (cos²A − sin²A)(cos²A + sin²A) = cos²A − sin²A = (1 − sin²A) − sin²A = 1 − 2 sin²A.

questions.q: If x = a cos θ + b sin θ and y = b cos θ − a sin θ, show that x² + y² = a² + b².
questions.answer:
x² = a²cos²θ + 2ab sin θ cos θ + b²sin²θ.
y² = b²cos²θ − 2ab sin θ cos θ + a²sin²θ.
Add: the middle terms cancel: x² + y² = a²(cos²θ + sin²θ) + b²(sin²θ + cos²θ) = a² + b².

questions.q: Evaluate tan 7° tan 23° tan 67° tan 83° − sec²45°.
questions.answer:
tan 83° = cot 7°, tan 67° = cot 23°, so the product = 1.
sec 45° = √2 ⇒ sec²45° = 2.
Value = 1 − 2 = −1.

questions.q: Prove that tan θ + cot θ = sec θ cosec θ.
questions.answer: tan θ + cot θ = sin θ/cos θ + cos θ/sin θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = sec θ cosec θ.

questions.q: If sin θ = 3/5, evaluate cos θ cot θ.
questions.answer:
Opposite 3, hypotenuse 5 ⇒ adjacent 4.
cos θ = 4/5, cot θ = 4/3.
cos θ cot θ = 16/15.

questions.q: Prove that (sec A − 1)/(sec A + 1) = (1 − cos A)/(1 + cos A).
questions.answer:
Write sec A = 1/cos A: (1/cos A − 1)/(1/cos A + 1).
Multiply numerator and denominator by cos A: (1 − cos A)/(1 + cos A).

questions.q: Prove that (sin θ − cos θ + 1)/(sin θ + cos θ − 1) = 1/(sec θ − tan θ).
questions.answer:
Divide numerator and denominator by cos θ: (tan θ − 1 + sec θ)/(tan θ + 1 − sec θ).
In the numerator replace 1 by sec²θ − tan²θ: numerator = (sec θ + tan θ) − (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sec θ + tan θ).
So the fraction = (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sec θ + tan θ)/(tan θ + 1 − sec θ) = sec θ + tan θ.
And 1/(sec θ − tan θ) = (sec θ + tan θ)/(sec²θ − tan²θ) = sec θ + tan θ. Proved.

questions.q: If tan θ = 1/√7, find (cosec²θ − sec²θ)/(cosec²θ + sec²θ).
In △ABC right-angled at B, AB = 7 cm and AC − BC = 1 cm. Find sin A, cos A and tan C.
questions.answer:
Let BC = x; AC = x + 1. (x + 1)² = x² + 49 ⇒ 2x + 1 = 49 ⇒ x = 24.
BC = 24 cm, AC = 25 cm.
sin A = BC/AC = 24/25; cos A = AB/AC = 7/25; tan C = AB/BC = 7/24.
